ANCHOR STORIES — Morning edition, Wednesday 22 July 2026

GEO
1. US ELEVENTH night of strikes on Iran; Trump threatens Natanz "Pickaxe Mountain" enrichment site "very heavily"; US toll 18; Hegseth says war cost $37.5bn. [BBC, AJ, CNN]
2. Rubio says Iran "not serious about talks"; strikes continue but "talks between our countries are continuing"; 10-day truce unaccepted. [CNN 7/22]
3. Oil near $92/93 as Houthis turn back Saudi tankers (Red Sea blockade); Kazakhstan halts Black Sea exports (4th tanker strike). [CNBC, AJ]
4. Ukraine 400-drone raid on Moscow region (oil depot); Russia's heavy Kyiv barrage. [ISW]
5. France record wildfires — 2 firefighters killed near Bordeaux; 42,000 ha burned, worst since WWII. [BBC]

UK
1. Burnham caps single bus fares at £2 from January (through 2027) — 2nd cost-of-living act. [ITV, Independent]
2. Inflation falls to 2.6% (15-month low) on cheaper June fuel; economists warn Nov peak ~3.4%. [BBC, ONS]
3. Economists (IFS) warn giveaways funded by unmade savings point to autumn tax rises; June borrowing £16bn. [Independent, BBC]
4. Gilts hold near 5% (two-month high), sterling ~$1.34, ahead of BoE 30 July. [market data, BBC]
5. Sacked Starmer loyalists restive on backbenches ("same gang, different seats"); Steve Reed letter. [Independent, BBC]

MARKETS (LIVE Wed): Brent $92.95 (+2.1%, extending rebound); Gold $4,118 record; GBP 1.3371 (<$1.34, 1-wk low); Gilt ~5.04%; FTSE/S&P/VIX = Tue closes (US shut); BTC ~$66,284.
